overall: The AG found the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: it declined to review non-OML allegations (materials, pre-meeting outreach, continuance, public hearing participation) and found Zoom and telephone access adequate.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly did not provide meeting materials, or cause them to be provided to the public, before its May 20 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: These allegations, even if true, do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly did not meet virtually with members of the public before the May 20 meeting to discuss access issues.
allegations.key_passage: These allegations, even if true, do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly did not continue the May 20 meeting until the complainant's access concerns could be addressed.
allegations.key_passage: These allegations, even if true, do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Meeting allegedly was not accessible to the public through virtual and telephone means, as required by the COVID-19 executive order.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Commission provided the public with adequate, alternative means of access to its May 20 meeting through Zoom and telephone in compliance with the Open Meeting Law and the Executive Order.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly failed to reasonably accommodate residents lacking virtual technology and elderly or disabled residents, such as those with sight or hearing impairment.
allegations.key_passage: the Complainant has not asserted that anyone was unable to access the meeting due to disability.

allegations.summary: Complainant objected to how public participation was handled during the public hearing portion of the May 20 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern the requirements for conducting a public hearing nor does it guarantee a right to participate in a public hearing, and we therefore decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether any actions taken by the Commission could be a violation of any separate law or regulation governing public hearings.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
